subject.title: fix(doctor): preserve allowlist entries for version-bound runtime plugins during stale config scan

question: Should `codex` be permanently exempt from stale `plugins.allow` pruning whenever it is undiscovered, or preserved only while a version-bound externalization install or migration is actively required?
rationale: The patch changes upgrade cleanup semantics for a user-owned allowlist and can retain stale configuration forever; source inspection cannot determine the intended compatibility lifetime.

options.title: Bound preservation to migration state
options.body: Preserve `codex` only when runtime configuration, a successful or failed install attempt, or explicit release migration state proves it is still required.

options.title: Adopt a permanent exception
options.body: Keep `codex` unconditionally exempt and explicitly accept that doctor will no longer prune this stale allowlist ID while the exception exists.

options.title: Pause for generic lifecycle metadata
options.body: Hold the PR until version-bound external plugins expose generic metadata that doctor can use without a core ID-specific preservation rule.

recommendation.title: Bound preservation to migration state
recommendation.body: Preserve `codex` only when runtime configuration, a successful or failed install attempt, or explicit release migration state proves it is still required.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent work is the strongest visible ownership signal across plugin doctor diagnostics, runtime requirement collection, and missing-plugin repair.
